results.content: # U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas prices spiked, squeezing Americans' finances. WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas prices spiked in the wake of renewed fighting in the Middle East, underscoring the affordability challenges that are top of mind for many voters with midterm elections now just seven weeks away. The consumer price index rose 3.4% last month compared with a year ago, the Labor Department said Friday, the same as in July. But on a monthly basis, inflation quickened, as costs jumped 0.4% from July to August, up from an increase of just 0.1% the previous month. results.content: Consumer sentiment plunged in September amid heightened inflation fears, hitting its second-lowest level on record in the University of Michigan’s monthly survey released Friday. The survey’s headline index hit a level of 47.8, down 7.5% from the August reading and off 13.2% from a year ago. This was the second-lowest reading on record for data going back to 1952 — the bottom coming in May as rising prices also jolted the outlook. Indeed, the one-year inflation outlook surged to 4.6%, up 0.6 percentage point from the prior level and the highest since hitting the same level in June. results.content: **In Brief:** A new survey of American travelers found that concerns about household finances and a possible recession increased, but travel activity remained above year-earlier levels. According to Future Partners’ latest State of the American Traveler study, American travelers reported a more cautious financial outlook in September. The share who said their household was financially better off than a year earlier declined to 32.8%, from 34.0% in the previous month. About 45.0% of travelers expected their financial situation to improve over the next 12 months, down from 46.1% in the prior month and 47.1% a year earlier.
